--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.select_edges_by_id()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Select edges by their IDs. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.select_edges_by_id()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Select edges by their IDs. title: >- [Graph.select_edges_by_id()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Select edges by their IDs. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Select edges by their IDs. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L23385-L23481){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.select_edges_by_id( edge_ids, set_op="union", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Select edges by id](../assets/graphs/select-edges-by-id.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A six-node grid whose seven edges are labeled with their integer ids 1 to 7. After select_edges_by_id with ids 2 and 5, the edges B–C and C–F are selected and drawn in the accent color." width="100%"} Selects the given edges. Edge IDs are internal integer identifiers assigned when edges are created; they can be listed with `get_edge_ids()`, read from the `id` column of `get_edge_df()`, or obtained from methods that return edge IDs. Use this when you already know exactly which edges you want to act on, for example to: - turn the output of a query or a filtered edge DataFrame into a selection for `set_edge_attrs_ws()`, `delete_edges_ws()`, or `rev_edge_dir_ws()` - re-apply a selection saved earlier with `get_selected_edge_ids()` The edges are added to the current selection, unless `set_op=` says otherwise, and duplicate IDs are ignored. Any node selection is cleared, since the graph holds a selection of nodes or of edges but not both. The graph is modified in place and returned for chaining. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edge_ids]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of integer edge IDs to select. Every ID must belong to an existing edge; a missing ID raises `KeyError` and leaves the selection unchanged. An empty list is allowed (with `set_op="replace"`, it clears the selection). [set_op]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["union"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : How these edges combine with the current edge selection. `"union"` (default) adds them to it, `"replace"` makes them the selection, `"intersect"` keeps only the selected edges among them, and `"difference"` removes them from it. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The same graph (modified in place) for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [EdgeNotFoundError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If any edge ID doesn't exist in the graph (a subclass of both `KeyError` and `ValueError`). [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `set_op=` is not `"union"`, `"replace"`, `"intersect"`, or `"difference"`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Edge IDs are assigned in creation order, so the first two IDs in this triangle belong to `A-B` and `B-C`. Selecting them leaves `C-A` unselected: ::: {#e030cd62 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A")]) ) edge_ids = graph.get_edge_ids() graph.select_edges_by_id(edge_ids=[edge_ids[0], edge_ids[1]]) graph.count_selected_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: A common pattern is to filter the edge DataFrame with Polars and pass the matching IDs back in. Here the edges heavier than `1.0` are selected and then shown with `get_edge_df_ws()`: ::: {#ee1720dd .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B", 0.5), ("B", "C", 2.0), ("C", "A", 3.5)]) ) heavy = graph.get_edge_df().filter(pl.col("weight") > 1.0)["id"].to_list() graph.select_edges_by_id(heavy) graph.get_edge_df_ws() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
